requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1.
requirements.summary: Direct observations show /dev/vgdata/lvdata mounted as XFS at /srv/data, initially at 1024 MiB and still mounted after growth and restart.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB without unmounting it.
requirements.summary: The mount identity remained 119:252:0 before and after the online operation; lvextend and xfs_growfs completed, leaving the LV at 2304 MiB and the mounted filesystem at 2.3 GiB.

requirements.requirement: Keep the mounted volume's contents intact during growth.
requirements.summary: The payload SHA-256 was identical before and after growth, and its contents remained directly readable. The same checksum and contents were also recovered after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence of an online expansion from 1 GiB to 2.25 GiB, continuous mounting, and preserved content. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: it includes a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot ID corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service, mount, LV, filesystem, loop device, and payload state.
limitations: The final lifecycle snapshot reports one failed LVM pvscan unit, although direct post-restart checks show the required volume and activation service healthy.
Package-manager consistency was unavailable both before and after execution, so the health of the mixed RHEL/CentOS package installation cannot be independently confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: No executor command mutation was clearly unnecessary: installing LVM and its temporary package source, creating the loop-backed PV/VG/LV, configuring persistent activation and mounting, and rebooting all had evidence-supported roles. The initially unprivileged repository write failed without evidence of mutation (cmd-1377cbeb408d4a53). Hygiene is reduced because an executor-caused lvm2-pvscan@7:0.service remained failed after completion, despite the intended activation service and storage being healthy. The added CentOS Vault repository was disabled after installation but retained; package consistency could not be independently checked.
